finding.claim: The /logo handler fetches a user-supplied URL after only a substring check (strings.Contains(raw, "example.io")). The check does not constrain the scheme, host or port. The attacker can pass e.g. http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/?x=example.io, http://127.0.0.1:8081/cdn#example.io, or http://example.io.attacker.com/. The server fetches the URL, follows redirects (default client) and returns the full response body to the attacker, so this is a full-read SSRF.
finding.sink: http.Get(raw) at main.go:36, with the response streamed back via io.Copy(w, resp.Body)

trace.note: raw := r.FormValue("logo") takes the attacker-controlled URL
Only check is strings.Contains(raw, "example.io"). It is unanchored and not parsed, so the substring can sit in the path, query, fragment, userinfo or a subdomain of an attacker domain
http.Get(raw) uses the default client, which follows redirects and has no IP or host restriction
The response body is copied back to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: Substring check on the raw string only; this is bypassable. No url.Parse, no host allowlist, no scheme check, no private-IP or dial-time check, and redirects are not disabled. Compare the /cdn handler, which does parse and check the exact hostname.

verdict.guard_found: Only strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") at main.go:32 (substring check, not a closing guard); no url.Parse, host allowlist, scheme check, or redirect restriction in /logo.
verdict.reason: main.go:31 takes the attacker-controlled "logo" param, main.go:32 only does an unanchored substring check that is bypassable (e.g. http://127.0.0.1/?x=example.io), and main.go:36-38 fetches it with the default redirect-following http.Get and copies the full body back to the caller.
